text:
Montreal's fourth straight win came with a first period that did most of the work: Cole Caufield scored at 7:24, Alex Newhook added one at 16:05, and Caufield struck again 27 seconds later to make it 3-1. Newhook, drafted 16th overall by Colorado in 2019 out of the Victoria Grizzlies, scored again in the second period, and by the time Dallas got going the Canadiens had a lead that stood up.

The shot totals suggest a tighter game than the score. MTL had 45 shot attempts to DAL's 38, and Dallas actually held the edge in the second period, 0.92 to 0.69 in expected goals (the quality of chances, not just the count). Montreal got the better of the third, 2.29 to 0.48 in that measure, and Phillip Danault's empty-net-free goal at 19:12 made it 5-2. Overall we have MTL at 4.12 expected goals to DAL's 2.11, and our simulations of every shot give the Canadiens a 64 percent chance to win, so the result was fair. Jake Oettinger allowed 1.1 goals more than the shots he faced deserved, while Jakub Dobes stopped 17 of 19 behind a team that gave away the puck 20 times.

Dallas went 1 for 3 on the power play, Wyatt Johnston scoring the goal with Mikko Rantanen and Miro Heiskanen assisting, and Jamie Benn cut it to 4-2 in the second. Montreal, 0 for 4 with the man advantage, didn't need it and moves on riding a four-game winning streak. Dallas leaves with the loss and a long look at its goaltending numbers.
